topArticle.title: Men deported from US bound and beaten in Equatorial Guinea detention hotel, lawyers say
topArticle.description:
Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence

Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers.
The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.
 Continue reading...
topArticle.titleJa: 弁護士によると、米国から強制送還された男性らが赤道ギニアの拘束ホテルで縛られ殴打された

topArticle.title: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died
topArticle.description:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children
Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.
The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.
 Continue reading...

topArticle.title: ‘We demand the truth’: Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee lead calls for proof of life of disappeared Eritrean writers
topArticle.description:
More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki
More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001.
Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter organised by PEN International and dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.

Bachelet, 74, announced ⁠her decision in a video posted on Instagram on Saturday, saying: “I will now continue, with the ⁠same determination as always, my international work.”

topArticle.title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
topArticle.description:
New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat
A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century.
The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.
 Continue reading...

Europe live – latest updates

topArticle.title: Aztec document goes on display in Mexico after 186 years abroad
topArticle.description: France's national library is lending the manuscript recounting the history of the Aztecs to Mexico.

topArticle.summary: フランス国立図書館がアステカの歴史を綴る写本をメキシコに貸与。186年ぶりにメキシコで公開される歴史的文書の展示について。文化遺産の里帰りとして注目を集めている。

topArticle.title: Colombia and Brazil deadliest countries for environmental activists, report says
topArticle.description: The two countries accounted for 52% of killings of environmental activists in 2025, according to Global Witness.

topArticle.summary: グローバル・ウィットネスの報告書が、2025年に環境活動家の殺害の52%がコロンビアとブラジルで発生したと指摘。両国における活動家の命の危険性を強調している。

topArticle.title: Maduro ally pleads guilty in $195m money laundering case in US court
topArticle.description: Alex Saab, a former aide to the ex-Venezuelan president, agrees to "co-operate fully" with US prosecutors.
topArticle.titleJa: マドゥロ元大統領の側近、米国裁判所で1億9500万ドルのマネーロンダリング事件で有罪を認める
topArticle.summary: ベネズエラの元大統領側近アレックス・サーブ氏が、米国での1億9500万ドルのマネーロンダリング事件で有罪を認め、検察との全面協力に合意。政治的な汚職問題として注目される。

topArticle.title: Trump's response is key as Argentina's Falklands demands get louder
topArticle.description: With Argentina's President Milei promising "winds of change" over the Falklands, will Donald Trump shift his stance on British rule?
topArticle.titleJa: アルゼンチンのフォークランド諸島要求が高まる中、トランプ氏の対応が鍵に
topArticle.summary: アルゼンチンのフォークランド諸島要求が強まる中、ミレイ大統領の「変化の風」の約束と、トランプ氏の英国支配への姿勢変更が鍵となる。

topArticle.title: Ecuador detains former minister José Serrano after U.S. deportation
topArticle.description: Deported from the United States, Ecuador’s former “superminister” now faces grave criminal investigations and political accusations in a justice system facing questions over due process.

topArticle.summary: 米国から強制送還されたエクアドルの元「スーパー大臣」ホセ・セラーノが拘束され、重大な刑事捜査と政治的告発に直面。司法制度の適正手続きに疑問符が投げかけられている。

topArticle.title: Weaponizing citizenship: Silencing dissent in Nicaragua
topArticle.description: In this edition, we examine an authoritarian narrative making the case for denationalization in Nicaragua.

topArticle.summary: ニカラグアで、異議申し立てを封じるために市民権剥奪が正当化される権威主義的言説について検証。「市民権の武器化」としてその実態を明らかにする。

topArticle.title: Swimmer killed in shark attack off Australian west coast
topArticle.description: Emergency crews rushed to Sorrento Beach in Perth after witnesses reported a man being dragged under by a shark.

topArticle.summary: パース沖のソレントビーチで男性がサメに襲われ死亡。目撃者の通報を受け、緊急隊が出動した悲劇的な事故。
